recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes the remaining current core source defect for FHIR-36933; no further core source change is recommended unless a later work-group decision changes jurisdiction UsageContext representation.
issue_request: FHIR-36933 was Applied/Persuasive and asked to add a jurisdiction usage-context type and include the Jurisdiction value set for usageContext when it is used outside base canonical-resource jurisdiction elements, such as in extensions and obligations.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-36933-tagged source commit was found. The current source already includes the Jurisdiction value set in ValueSet/use-context and uses the THO usage-context-type jurisdiction code implemented by UP-459. The later FHIR-45507 source addition created UsageContext-additional-bindings.xml with a jurisdiction conditional binding; subsequent fixes repaired XML structure and THO URLs, but the jurisdiction binding purpose remained misspelled as exetensible.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes show the issue was first resolved in 2022 by choosing a jurisdiction extension, then reopened and approved 8-0-0 on 2023-08-21. Zulip discussion identified the R5 jurisdiction/useContext inconsistency and missing THO usage-context-type code, which UP-459 then implemented. FHIR-38841 is a same-family topic/jurisdiction UsageContext migration issue already represented on the combined branch, and FHIR-39632 confirms core should point usage-context-type references at THO.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes/UsageContext-additional-bindings.xml so the jurisdiction binding purpose is extensible instead of exetensible. The existing jurisdiction value-set include and external THO code were left unchanged.
source_changes: source/datatypes/UsageContext-additional-bindings.xml: corrected the uc-bind-jurisdiction purpose from exetensible to extensible.
